answer: Sybil resistance rests on one concrete mechanism: a per-identity bond locked before an agent earns anything, with its price rising superlinearly as more identities trace back to the same operator graph. Fifty fake agents demand fifty full bonds, the last costlier than the first, so mass registration outweighs honest work. Bonds stay locked for epochs, freezing capital, and early exits burn part of the stake. Each fable of "many independent voices" collapses into one payer: an island of a single wallet ringed by receipts pointing home, forcing the attacker to forge real value, not accounts.
